title: Aśokan patronage at Sanchi
summary: The beginnings of Sanchi as a Buddhist sacred centre are attributed to the Mauryan emperor Aśoka. A pillar and brick stupa were followed by additions over many later periods.

claims.text: The beginnings of Sanchi as a Buddhist sacred centre are attributed to the Mauryan emperor Aśoka. A pillar and brick stupa were followed by additions over many later periods.
Third-century BCE attribution; individual surviving components are often later.

Patronage links religious institutions with political power, but the monuments did not emerge in one completed form. Later enlargements should remain distinguishable from the early foundation associated with Aśoka.
